title: S2a1 memory_hot: bounded HOT memory view generated from the store, never-compact classes, deterministic compaction, memory hot/compact CLI (P1 HOT, P4)
spec:
Create orchestrator/memory_hot.py on top of memory_store (S1a). Config in pool.toml [memory]: hot_budget_tokens = 3000 (dated comment; tokens estimated as chars/4 like skills_registry._token_estimate), hot_never_compact = ["gotcha:open", "architecture", "decision:constraint", "decision:security"] (gotcha:open means a gotcha whose outcome is empty or contains unresolved or open; decision:<tag> means a decision carrying that tag; the config list is the single source of the pin rule), hot_recent_days = 14. build(root, budget_tokens=None) -> {"records": [...], "tokens": n, "dropped": [ids], "pinned": [ids]}: candidates = every warm record, read through a new memory_store.all_records(root, tier=None) helper (no limit; add it in memory_store.py, scope below), never through search() whose limit defaults to 20; pinned (never compacted) = architecture records, gotchas whose outcome is empty or says unresolved/open, decisions tagged constraint or security, and any record for which ANY id in its source_tasks list names a bus task whose status is one of queued, held, running (an open-status allowlist; done, failed, superseded, unknown ids and any other value count as closed); the rest ranked by score = recency (days since date, decaying over hot_recent_days) + kind weight (gotcha 3, decision 2, architecture 2, model_note 1, retrospective 1, strategy 1, skill_outcome 1, reference 1) + 1 per open bus task whose title or scope mentions one of the record's components; fill the budget by score after the pinned set; if the pinned set alone exceeds the budget, keep it and report over_budget = true (never drop pinned). Each record is rendered as one compact line (date, kind, title, and for gotchas the first sentence of the body) plus a pointer line 'memory show <id>' only for governing decisions that were dropped. Writes .orchestrator/memory/HOT.md with a first line stating it is generated by memory_hot and must not be edited, and marks the chosen records tier hot in the store (all others hot -> warm; cold unchanged). compact(root) = build and rewrite; idempotent. CLI: `orchestrator memory hot [--json]` (prints the view and the budget report), `orchestrator memory compact` (rebuilds HOT.md, prints pinned/dropped counts). Run migrate + compact against this repository's real memory files and report the token count and the pinned/dropped counts in the result and in docs/hermes-hardening/07-hot-memory.md. Do not touch spawn.py: packets are wired in the next task.
Spec review T-1064 folded in: open-status allowlist for pinning on ANY source_tasks id; reference weight 1; unbounded candidate read via memory_store.all_records; the merged Record field is source_tasks (list).
Spec reviews T-1077 and T-1079 folded in: (a) memory_store.py gains all_records(root=ROOT, tier=None) and set_tiers(mapping, root=ROOT) (same root=ROOT default convention as the other functions); build() marks tiers through set_tiers; rebuild() resets tiers to warm/cold, so docs and the memory rebuild CLI output say to run memory compact afterwards, and compact() is what restores hot marks. (b) Open bus tasks are read ONCE per build() into a set (resolve ids the way memory_store._goal_from_bus does: bus.get when root is ROOT, else read root/.orchestrator/tasks/<id>.json, catching KeyError and FileNotFoundError; an id that cannot be found is closed); that one set serves both pinning (ANY source_tasks id in the open set, statuses queued/held/running only; the test fixture uses task files with status done and an id that does not exist to cover the closed cases) and the +1 score term. (c) Component match semantics for the score term: case-insensitive whole-token match of the component name against the task title split on non-word characters and against scope path basenames without extension. (d) HOT.md's generated header is static text with no date or timestamp, so a second run is byte-identical. (e) In pool.toml put the hot_* keys under a comment line separating them from the progressive-recall keys in the same [memory] table. (f) Acceptance test test_pinned_classes_never_dropped also covers a security-tagged decision and a gotcha with an empty outcome and one whose outcome says open.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_pinned_classes_never_dropped (unresolved gotcha, architecture, constraint decision and open-task records survive a tiny budget with over_budget true)
tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_budget_fill_by_score_and_tier_marks (higher-score records chosen first; store tiers updated; HOT.md written with the generated header)
tests/test_memory_hot.py::test_pinning_uses_open_status_allowlist_on_any_source_task (superseded and unknown ids do not pin; a running one does)
